title: Sell Mineral Rights in Portal, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Portal, ND
metaDescription: Mineral rights near Portal, ND at the border crossing? Burke County has flank-area Bakken history worth checking. Get an honest offer.
heroLead: Portal is best known as a border crossing, but the Burke County ground around it carries mineral rights that a surprising number of families still hold without ever having looked closely at what's underneath.
intro: Burke County sits on the northern flank of the Bakken, and while it's never drawn the attention that McKenzie or Mountrail County has, operators have drilled here over the years and some Portal-area tracts have real, if modest, production history attached to them.

sections.heading: What's actually been drilled near Portal
paragraphs: Burke County has seen periodic horizontal Bakken activity, generally with more variable results than the core counties further south. Some sections near Portal have producing wells; others nearby have none. We check the state well index for your specific tract rather than assuming based on the county's general reputation.

sections.heading: Border-crossing town, ordinary title work
paragraphs: Despite Portal's unusual position right on the international border, the mineral rights title process here is the same as anywhere else in North Dakota. We pull the Burke County Recorder's records to confirm ownership and legal description before making any offer.

sections.heading: What we've found researching Burke County tracts
paragraphs: Burke County's oil-and-gas activity clusters unevenly, with some sections seeing multiple horizontal wells and others nearby untouched. Families who inherited acreage near Portal often assume their interest matches a neighbor's, when the actual well history can be quite different.
That's why we always check your exact legal description against the state's well and permit index rather than lean on general reputation for the area.

faqs.question: Does Portal's location right on the border change anything about selling minerals?
faqs.answer: No. The mineral rights themselves are governed by North Dakota law and Burke County recording the same as anywhere else in our coverage area.

faqs.question: We think a well might be near our property but aren't sure. Can you check?
faqs.answer: Yes, send us your legal description and we'll check the state's well index and permitting records for anything on or near your tract.

faqs.question: What if there's no current lease on our Portal property?
faqs.answer: We can still make an offer on unleased minerals. It simply changes how we approach valuing the interest compared to a producing, leased tract.

faqs.question: How do we know if a neighboring section's activity applies to our tract?
faqs.answer: It usually doesn't automatically. Well spacing units are legally defined, so we check whether your specific acreage is actually pooled into a producing unit rather than assume based on nearby drilling.
